liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Terrapin Station** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Judged one of the best Terrapins the reviewer has heard, with a tight band; Watched from the balcony and called it the best Terrapin ever seen, truly uplifting [7][20][22]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review, 1 other source): Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance is singled out as quite nice; The first 0:20 of Lost Sailor is missing from the soundboard [1][17]
- **Ship Of Fools** (1 review): Reviewer's favorite version; Jerry's lead vocal and the backing vocals sound especially good [17]
- **Drums** (1 other source): A 1:02 patch in Drums comes from a Beyer M160 source via Frank Streeter [2]
- **The Other One** (1 review): The Space leading into The Other One runs very long [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-02-28.154897.mtx.seamons.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 26 songs; 191 min [1]. Said about its sound: The soundboard source had noise reduction, hotter levels and brittleness; Streeter's tape turns muffled at the encore [1]
- **gd1981-02-28.178981.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 25 songs; 196 min [2]
- **gd1981-02-28.naks.mason.128747.flac16**: source not stated; 25 songs; 197 min [4]
- **gd81-02-28.sbd.lutch.4668.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 25 songs; 179 min; rated 3.74/5 by 23 [6]. Said about its sound: Faint hiss, audible mainly in quiet instrumental passages or when the treble is boosted high; Recording is crisp and clear, with Jerry's playing and singing well captured; Among the best recordings in the reviewer's collection, very crisp [15][18][20][21]
- **gd1981-02-28.151914.sbd.mcgee.chief.miller.clugston.flac16**: soundboard; 25 songs; 182 min [7]
- **gd81-02-28.glassberg.steinthal-cohen-vernon.20345.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 24 songs; 193 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [10]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds warm, clean and fairly crisp [26]

## Around the show

- Attendee remembers the small, atmospheric Uptown as a favorite venue; this was the last night of the run [22]
- Brent's keyboard sound on the synthesizer is likened to Keith Emerson's Moog playing [23]
- Reviewer notes the Uptown Theater in Chicago is empty and decaying but still impressively large outside [26]
- Rated below all-time greats such as 5/8/77 and 5/24/72 [17]
- Considered a top example of the best early-1980s Dead [18]
- Part of a three-night run in which every show has impeccable sound and playing [19]
- Reviewer picks this night over the other two in the run [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-02-28.154897.mtx.seamons.flac16**: source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro [1]. Also: Matrix: Jim Wise soundboard via CDR, with Glassberg audience for set 1 and encore, Streeter's tape for set 2 [1]
- **gd1981-02-28.178981.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Barry Glassberg's Master Audience Cassettes: Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TCD5M (Maxell UDXL II) [2]
- **gd1981-02-28.naks.mason.128747.flac16**: taped by Mason B. Taylor; source: Recorded By Mason Taylor on a Nakamichi 550 Cassette Deck, on chrome tapes, with Nakamichi microphones; Transferred on Mason's restored Nak550 properly [4]. Also: Taped by Chicago taper Mason B. Taylor using a Nakamichi 550 and Nakamichi 300 mics with shotgun capsules [4]
- **gd81-02-28.sbd.lutch.4668.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Dick Latvala; source: Soundboard [6]. Also: Soundboard transfer was remastered by Jim Wise [16]
- **gd1981-02-28.151914.sbd.mcgee.chief.miller.clugston.flac16**: taped by David McGee and Chief; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > ? > DAT (16/44.1k) [7]
- **gd81-02-28.glassberg.steinthal-cohen-vernon.20345.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by John Steinthal; source: Audience Recording: Nak700>Sony TCD5M, Maxell UDXLII, Dolby B [10]
